xtb.name: XTB
xtb.guide: In xStation open Account history → Cash operations, choose a period starting at your first trade, click Export and pick the CSV format.
xtb.note: The file also contains deposits, dividends and fees – only purchases and sales of stocks and ETFs are imported. We fill in the currency from the exchange.

trading212.name: Trading 212
trading212.guide: In the app open History → the export icon, tick Orders, choose a period and download the CSV.
trading212.note: One export covers at most 12 months – upload several files, we recognise duplicates.

degiro.name: Degiro
degiro.guide: On the website open Activity → Transactions, set a period starting at your first trade and click Export → CSV. Do not use the account statement (Account statement).

ibkr.name: Interactive Brokers
ibkr.guide: In Client Portal open Performance & Reports → Flex Queries, create an Activity Flex Query with the Trades section and the fields Symbol, ISIN, TradeDate, Buy/Sell, Quantity, TradePrice, CurrencyPrimary, AssetClass and TradeID, format CSV, and run it for the whole period.

moony.name: Your own table (Moony template)
moony.guideTitle: How to fill in the table
moony.guide: Download the template, fill it in in Excel or another spreadsheet and save it as CSV.
moony.excel: A file saved by Excel in any language works as it is – we detect the delimiter, the encoding and the decimal mark. Moony's own export (Stocks → Export) has the same format.
